stories.headline: Tensions Rise Between US and Iran as Trump Threatens Oman
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump has threatened to bomb Oman if the nation interferes with American negotiations with Iran, according to a report by Fox News. The threat comes at a time of severe tension across the Middle East as military actions expand.

In Iraq, violent attacks have directly targeted political and security leaders. Two Hadid-110 drones launched from Iranian territory struck the office of Kurdistan Regional Government Prime Minister Masrour Barzani, as well as the residence of a regional security chief. United States Ambassador to Iraq Tom Barrack strongly condemned these drone strikes in Iraqi Kurdistan, calling them a direct threat to regional stability.

At the diplomatic level, statements from officials remain conflicted. A spokesperson for the Iranian news agency Tasnim publicly denied President Donald Trump's claim that the United States maintains a direct backchannel with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. However, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei stated that Iran and Oman have reached an understanding on transit route maps through the strategic Strait of Hormuz. The passage is vital for global energy supplies, as approximately one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas passes through the Strait of Hormuz.

The ongoing conflict is causing significant economic impact both in the Middle East and inside the United States. Hotel occupancy in Dubai fell drastically from 80 percent to around 10 percent after Iran launched strikes against allies of the United States in response to previous US-Israel attacks. In response to the crisis, the United Arab Emirates introduced a $680 million economic package to support local businesses affected by the Iran war. Meanwhile, consumers in the United States are facing higher costs, as US gasoline prices rose by nearly a third compared to one year earlier, according to the American Automobile Association.

These developments coincide with rising domestic political pressure on the American administration. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 80 percent of Americans believe that US involvement in Iran will continue for an extended period. The same Reuters/Ipsos poll showed that President Donald Trump's approval rating has dropped to 33 percent, which matches the lowest point of his presidency.

stories.headline: Trump Orders Scale-Back of US Military Drills in South Korea
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump has announced on Truth Social that the United States will substantially reduce its joint military exercises with South Korea. Trump explicitly linked this decision to scale back the joint drills to South Korea's refusal to assist in American military operations regarding Iran. Approximately 28,500 American military personnel are currently stationed in South Korea.

Despite President Trump's order to reduce the exercises, joint military drills between South Korea and the United States proceeded as scheduled on Monday. In response to the announcement, South Korea's presidential Blue House stated that it would review Donald Trump's comments while continuing diplomatic consultations with Washington.

The military policy shift follows other diplomatic remarks made by the US president. Speaking in the Oval Office, Donald Trump stated that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un responded positively to his diplomatic overtures. Meanwhile, US envoy Jared Kushner stated that progress toward Gaza demilitarization could materialize in as little as 30 days.

stories.headline: Gaza Ceasefire Talks Stall as Kushner Meets Regional Leaders
stories.body:
US envoy Jared Kushner has left Jerusalem without reaching a breakthrough after holding two days of diplomatic talks with Israeli and Hamas leaders. Before travelling to Jerusalem, Kushner met with Hamas political chief Khalil al-Hayya in Egypt. Despite the lack of a major deal, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jared Kushner agreed that an American general will oversee the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza. They also agreed to establish specialized working groups focused on Gaza's demilitarization and public health.

The diplomatic efforts take place as violence and political tension persist. Israeli military forces currently control approximately 60 percent of the Gaza Strip. Gaza's health ministry reported that at least 1,265 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli military operations since the ceasefire went into effect on October 10. Meanwhile, far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir stated in a podcast interview that Israel should kill 30 to 40 people every night in Gaza.

International criticism of Israel's stance has grown. Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Pakistan, and Indonesia issued a joint statement condemning Israel's rejection of the US-backed ceasefire proposal.

stories.headline: European Nations Deploy Emergency Support Amid Severe Wildfires
stories.body:
Wildfires and intense heatwaves are causing severe damage across Europe, leading to international emergency deployments. Data from the European Forest Fire Information System revealed that 576,000 hectares of land burned across Europe in 2026. The EU's Copernicus service confirmed that western Europe experienced its warmest June-to-July period on record.

Tragedies and evacuations have been reported in several countries. In Spain, a Spanish soldier died while battling the Peñas de Riglos wildfire in the Aragón region. In Greece, two people died and hundreds were evacuated due to twin wildfires on the island of Salamina. In Germany, approximately 30 residents in the border town of Monschau received evacuation orders as High Fens wildfires approached. In France, 183 homes were destroyed in Le Porge, where French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu was heckled by residents during a visit. Lecornu announced €12 million in government aid for the Gironde and Landes regions.

European nations are sending aid to affected neighbors. Britain deployed military personnel to assist across Europe. France sent 104 firefighters and 36 emergency vehicles to Spain, while Germany, Sweden, Norway, and the Netherlands sent emergency aerial and ground reinforcements to Belgium.

stories.headline: Ebola Epidemic in Democratic Republic of Congo Becomes Deadliest Ever
stories.body:
An ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 2,325 people, making it the country's deadliest Ebola epidemic on record. The DRC Public Health Institute reported that total confirmed Ebola cases reached 4,945, with 101 new cases detected in just 24 hours. More than 3,400 of these confirmed cases were recorded in the DRC's Ituri province.

While the Democratic Republic of Congo battles the crisis, neighboring Uganda declared itself free of Ebola on July 28 after discharging its final treated patient.

International health organizations and medical researchers are working on vaccines to combat the disease. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated that two vaccines developed specifically for the Bundibugyo strain are currently undergoing clinical trials. Additionally, the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency granted approval for human trials of an Oxford University-developed vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo Ebola strain.

stories.headline: Deadly 7.7-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Eastern Indonesia
stories.body:
A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia shortly before 06:00 local time on Saturday, leaving at least 68 people dead and over 200 others injured. The quake hit Flores island at a depth of 15 kilometers. The surrounding East Nusa Tenggara province registered nearly 1,600 aftershocks following the major tremor.

The destruction from the earthquake has caused widespread displacement and strain on medical services. The disaster damaged more than 900 buildings and forced nearly 13,000 people from their homes. On Flores island, Dr. Melinda, the sole physician at the Dampek Health Centre, issued an urgent plea for help while treating hundreds of quake victims. During the crisis, a woman named Maria Florida Nogo Kelen underwent emergency C-section surgery to give birth as the earthquake struck.

stories.headline: BJP Announces Major Leadership Overhaul Under President Nitin Nabin
stories.body:
The Bharatiya Janata Party has announced a major national organizational reshuffle under President Nitin Nabin, replacing nearly 50 of the 65 office-bearers on its national team. The broad reorganization includes 12 women leaders in the newly announced national leadership team.

As part of the reshuffle, former Union minister Smriti Irani was appointed as a BJP national general secretary and placed in charge of Uttar Pradesh. This appointment follows political challenges in the state during recent elections. The party's vote share in Uttar Pradesh dropped significantly from around 50 percent in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections to approximately 41 percent in 2024.

Smriti Irani is one of eight leaders appointed as national general secretaries. The other newly named national general secretaries are Biplab Deb, Sunil Bansal, Vinod Tawde, Gajendra Patel, Satish Poonia, Harish Dwivedi, and Sanjay Bhatia. In another major appointment, Professor Tariq Mansoor, the former vice chancellor of Aligarh Muslim University, was named a BJP national vice president.

The party also made significant changes to its digital operations. Deepak Mhaskey was appointed as the BJP's new national social media convener, taking over the role from his long-serving predecessor Amit Malviya. Mhaskey previously worked as a college chemistry professor and served as the head of the BJP social media cell in the state of Chhattisgarh.

stories.headline: Jharkhand Cancels Recruitment Exams Following Widespread Student Protests
stories.body:
Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has announced the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL recruitment examination and all official activities associated with the testing agency TDPL. Following the announcement, student leader Devendra Nath Mahto ended his hunger strike after Chief Minister Soren agreed to cancel the disputed recruitment exams.

The decision followed intense student demonstrations across the state capital of Ranchi. Protesting students organized under the JPSC-JSSC Abhyarthi Nyay Manch and JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch platforms held sit-in protests at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where six students went on an indefinite hunger strike. National political support also emerged when Congress leader Rahul Gandhi sent a letter to CM Hemant Soren, urging him to meet directly with the demonstrating students.

In response to the protests and examination irregularities, the Jharkhand government ordered a comprehensive CID investigation into recruitment exam errors occurring since 2014. Additionally, the state government decided to form a dedicated examination reforms committee headed by senior IAS officer Amitabh Kaushal.
